newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PRESIDENT SAYS BALTIC ECONOMIES EQUAL.
newsitem.headline: PRESIDENT SAYS BALTIC ECONOMIES EQUAL.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said on Thursday that his country's economy was advancing and keeping pace with Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia.
Lithuania has been regarded as lagging behind its Baltic cousins, Estonia in particular, in the transition to a market economy.
But Brazauskas defended his country's economic record, pointing out that the macro picture compared favourably with Latvia and Estonia.
"All three Baltic countries enjoy equality in economic development," Brazauskas told Reuters in an interview.
"Lithuania's macroeconomic indicators are as good as Latvia and Estonia's and better in some areas," he added.
"Our inflation last year was 13.1 percent, the lowest among the Baltic countries, and our gross domestic product (GDP) growth was the highest," he said.
Preliminary economic data suggests that Lithuania's economy grew by four percent in 1996, the statistics department said.
Brazauskas said that Lithuania had resolved a number of key economic problems, including last year's crisis in the banking sector and currency stability.
He added that the all of the country's major political parties were committed to economic reforms.
"Despite the (recent) change in government...(our) foreign and domestic policies have remained the same," he added.
